difference_keeps_closedness.description: Trap: the complement keeps the subtrahend's closedness instead of flipping it, so [1,5] − [2,3] gives [1,2] + [3,5]. Masked when the subtrahend's ends are open.

equal_lower_takes_farther_flag.description: Trap: when two merged intervals share a lower bound, the one reaching farther supplies both flags instead of the lower flags being OR-ed, so [1,2] + (1,5) gives (1,5) rather than [1,5). Seen (combined with a lower-bound-only sort) in the calibration baseline runs. Masked when merged intervals never share a lower bound.

float_endpoints.description: Trap: bounds are converted to float internally, so Fraction and Decimal values come back changed. Masked while tests use ints.

halfopen_point_kept.description: Trap: lo == hi counts as non-empty when either end is closed, so (2,2] and [2,2) survive normalize and a difference by a half-open "point" removes a point. Masked unless degenerate half-open intervals appear.

intersection_closed_or.description: Trap: at an equal endpoint the intersection is closed when either input is closed (or instead of and). Masked when endpoints differ.

intersection_not_normalized.description: Trap: intersection is the raw pairwise product of the inputs, neither the inputs nor the result normalized, so [1,5] ∩ ([1,2] + [2,5]) comes back as two intervals. Masked when both inputs are already canonical.

merge_any_touching.description: Trap: intervals that touch (hi1 == lo2) always merge, even when both ends at the meeting point are open, so [1,3) + (3,5] becomes [1,5]. Masked when a closed end meets the point.

merge_only_overlapping.description: Trap: only strictly overlapping intervals (hi1 > lo2) merge; [1,3] + [3,5] stays two intervals. Masked when inputs overlap by more than a point.

no_validation.description: Trap: closed unbounded ends and non-bool flags are accepted (flags coerced with bool()). Masked by well-formed input.

point_dropped.description: Trap: lo == hi is always empty, so the closed point [3,3] disappears from normalize, intersection ([1,3] ∩ [3,5]) and difference results. Masked unless a point interval appears.

shorthand_halfopen.description: Trap: the 2-tuple shorthand is read as the half-open [lo, hi) like Python's range. Masked when tests use 4-tuples only.

sort_by_lower_only.description: Trap: the sweep sorts by lower bound only (input order on ties), so a closed point [3,3] listed after (3,5] is visited after it and the gap between [1,3) and (3,5] is never closed. Seen in the calibration baseline runs. Masked when equal lower bounds arrive closed-first.

unsorted_output.description: Trap: no sort; only neighbours in input order are merged and the output keeps input order. Masked when inputs arrive sorted.
